questions.stem: What are the three tiers of Lifecycle Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three tiers of lifecycle management are Know what you have (C - visibility/inventory), Improve management controls (D - governance), and Improve efficiency (E - optimization). These map to the foundational ITAM maturity progression.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow role enables the user to perform actions related to incident, problem, change, and configuration management?
questions.explanation: The itil role enables users to perform incident, problem, change, and configuration management actions. The the docs confirms 'Role required: itil' for Enterprise Asset Management incident actions including resolving and closing incidents.

questions.stem: Which plugins for asset management functionality are inactive by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Hardware Asset Management (B), Procurement (C), and Cost Management (E) are plugins inactive by default that must be explicitly activated. Expense Line and Depreciation are included in baseline Asset Management; My Assets is a standard portal module.

questions.stem: What is the third tier of the capability blueprint?
questions.explanation: The capability blueprint tiers are: Tier 1=Trustworthy data, Tier 2=Practical management, Tier 3=Operational integration (D), Tier 4=Financial management. The third tier is Operational integration.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a component of a hardware asset's lifecycle?
questions.explanation: The hardware asset lifecycle stages are Request, Procure, Receive, Deploy, Monitor, Service, and Retire/Dispose. 'Consume' (C) is a concept for consumable assets (stockroom items), not a stage in the hardware asset lifecycle.

questions.stem: The Hardware Asset Management (HAM) application expands baseline ITSM Asset Management with which features? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Hardware Asset Management expands baseline ITSM Asset Management with Hardware Model Normalization (C), Hardware Asset Dashboard (D), and Asset Inventory Audit (G). Stockrooms and Asset/Model Records exist in baseline ITSM; Mobile features are separate.

questions.stem: Expected outcomes of IT asset management (ITAM) include which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Integrates with business services via the Service Catalog from request through to disposal
Leverages IT Service Management (ITSM) to manage the lifecycle of assets as they pass through their useful life as configuration items (CIs)
Provides input into, aligns with, and follows corporate governance
Improves application privacy and security adherence
Leverages Service Mapping to predict service impact

questions.explanation: Expected ITAM outcomes include integrating with business services via Service Catalog from request to disposal (A), leveraging ITSM to manage the asset lifecycle as CIs (B), and providing input into corporate governance (C). Service Mapping (E) is ITSM/CMDB; application security (D) is APM.

questions.stem: What is the difference between ITAM personas and ITAM Roles? (Choose four.)

options.text: A user may have multiple roles, but a single persona
Roles control access to features in the product
Personas represent types of users of the product
Personas control access to features in the product
Roles represent types of users of the product
A user may have multiple roles and personas

questions.explanation: Roles control access to features (B), Personas represent types of users (C), a user may have multiple roles but a single persona (A), and a user may have multiple roles and personas (F) in workspace assignments. Roles and personas are complementary governance mechanisms.

questions.stem: Hamm is a member of the Asset Managers group which has the ham_admin role assigned to it. Based on this role alone, which of the following operations can Hamm perform? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Based on ham_admin alone, Hamm can revert normalization results (A), create and delete asset records (B), create purchase orders (C), and add Service Catalog entries (F) for hardware request flows. Creating flows (D) requires flow_designer; importing assets (E) requires additional roles.

questions.stem: What information would you track for a configuration item (CI) versus an asset? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: CIs track operational information (D - how it is configured and functioning) and relationships to other CIs (E). Assets track financial (A), lifecycle (B), and contractual (C) information. The CMDB is used for operational and relationship management.

questions.stem: A component is considered an IT asset vs. a configuration item (CI) when you want to do which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Manage its procurement, maintenance, or retirement
Track its monetary value or costs
Manage its associated license, warranty, or lease contracts
Know its relationships to other assets in the CMDB

questions.explanation: A component is treated as an IT asset when you want to manage procurement/maintenance/retirement (A), track monetary value/costs (C), or manage license/warranty/lease contracts (D). Tracking operational info (B) and CMDB relationships (E) define CI usage.

questions.stem: Which of the following are considered assets? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Facilities (A), hardware (C), and software entitlements (D) are considered assets tracked in the Asset table. Contracts (B) are separate contract records, not assets. Software distributions (E) are software media packages, not asset records.

questions.stem: What is the default display name for an asset?

options.text: An automatically generated combination of serial number and model category
An automatically generated combination of asset tag and model
An automatically generated combination of serial number and model
An automatically generated combination of asset tag and model category

questions.explanation: The default display name for an asset is an automatically generated combination of asset tag and model (B). The system property glide.cmdb_model.display_name.shorten controls model display name generation but the asset display name uses asset tag + model.

questions.stem: What is the default state of a newly created asset?
questions.explanation: The default state of a newly created asset record is In use (A). Assets change to In stock when received into a stockroom via procurement workflows, or In transit during transfer. A manually created asset record defaults to In use.

questions.stem: What is the impact of a customer opting out of the ServiceNow Content Service for specific models?

options.text: Unrecognized data doesn't get sent to the ServiceNow Content Service and the customer doesn't receive Content Library updates
Unrecognized data doesn't get sent to the ServiceNow Content Service
Unrecognized data is sent to the ServiceNow Content Service, but is now encrypted
Customer doesn't receive Content Library updates

questions.explanation: When a customer opts out of the ServiceNow Content Service for specific models, unrecognized data for those models is not sent to the Content Service (B). The customer still receives Content Library updates for other models that remain opted in.

questions.stem: What fields does the ServiceNow Content Service normalize or enrich? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The Content Service normalizes and enriches Lifecycle dates (A), Device type (B), Manufacturer (C), and Hardware model name/number (F). Memory (D) is a hardware specification not managed by the content service; Asset tag (E) is user-assigned.

questions.stem: What is the process of restructuring data to maintain consistency?
questions.explanation: Normalization is the process of restructuring data to maintain consistency. It standardizes manufacturer names, model names, device types, and lifecycle data against the Content Service library to ensure uniform, accurate records.

questions.stem: What are ways to measure trustworthy data? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four measures of trustworthy data are Credibility (C), Dependability (D), Transferability (E), and Reliability (F). These represent the standard ITAM framework for evaluating data quality and trustworthiness. Sustainability and Plausibility are not standard measures.

questions.stem: Any normalization that has occurred on a model can be reverted by using this feature.
questions.explanation: Normalization that has occurred on a model can be reverted using the Revert Normalization UI Action (D) on the model form. The scheduled normalization job only updates normalization fields and does not modify original fields like Model Name or Manufacturer.

questions.stem: Which of these tables are installed with Hardware Model Normalization? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Tables installed with Hardware Model Normalization include Device Type (A), Hardware Manufacturer (B), and Hardware Model Library (D). The the docs lists these as installed tables. Hardware Normalize Key and Device Name are not installed tables.

questions.stem: To perform hardware model normalization, which three fields from the hardware model record are used to set the normalized display name?

options.text: Name, Asset tracking unit, Model number
Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model category
Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model number

questions.explanation: The three fields used to set the normalized display name during hardware model normalization are Name (A), Manufacturer (B), and Model number (B). The the docs confirms the display name is generated from these three model fields.

questions.stem: What is the global standard for product recognition used during hardware model normalization?
questions.explanation: The global standard for product recognition used during hardware model normalization is UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code) (C). The the docs explicitly references UNSPSC for product classification in the content service.

questions.stem: During hardware model normalization, a hardware asset is set to a normalization status of, "Partially Normalized". What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The model name is missing from the hardware model record.
The model number is missing from the hardware model record.
The model product is missing from the hardware model record.
The model manufacturer is missing from the hardware model record.

questions.explanation: The most likely cause of a 'Partially Normalized' status is the missing model number (B) from the hardware model record. Partial normalization occurs when the manufacturer and product name match but the model number is absent, preventing full normalization.

questions.stem: What information should be tracked in an asset record? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An asset record tracks Financial information (B) and Contractual information (D). The the docs confirms the Asset table stores 'general, financial, and contractual information.' Physical, operational, and logical relationship data belongs in the CMDB/CI records.

questions.stem: Once the content update adds hardware lifecycle data to your instance, can it be deleted?

options.text: No, it cannot unless the lifecycle stage is EOL
Yes, it can be deleted or deactivated

questions.explanation: Hardware lifecycle data added by the weekly content update cannot be deleted (C). Content service-provided lifecycle data is system-managed and read-only, the same principle as in SAM. Customers can override values but cannot delete content-provided records.

questions.stem: What feature does the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) application use to fully normalize hardware models?
questions.explanation: Hardware Asset Management uses Normalization mappings (D) to fully normalize hardware models. These mappings compare model data against the HAM Content Service library to standardize manufacturer, product, and model information.

questions.stem: During normalization, what is the most common cause for hardware models to generate a status of Match Not Found?
questions.explanation: The most common cause of a 'Match Not Found' status during normalization is missing data (D) in the model record - such as incomplete manufacturer name, model name, or model number that prevents the system from finding a match in the Content Service library.

questions.stem: Which values does the "Asset tracking strategy" field provide to affect individual models? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three values for the Asset tracking strategy field are Create consumable asset (A), Don't create assets (B), and Leave to category (D). The the docs explicitly lists these as the options for this field.

questions.stem: When activating Hardware Asset Management (HAM) in an instance already running Field Service Management (FSM), how do you configure asset tasks for existing incident, change, and work order flows?

options.text: No configuration is required: asset tasks automatically activate behind the scenes
Activate HAM, then run scheduled job "Asset - Create FSM asset tasks" to insert the asset tasks
Activate HAM and then re-run the scheduled FSM jobs
Stop the scheduled FSM jobs, activate HAM, then restart the scheduled FSM jobs

questions.explanation: When activating Hardware Asset Management in an instance already running FSM, no configuration is required (A). Asset tasks automatically activate for existing incident, change, and work order flows behind the scenes upon HAM activation.

questions.stem: When a hardware asset is retired (e.g., a server), what happens to any existing software allocations on that asset?

options.text: The software allocations remain with the hardware asset and need to be reclaimed manually.
The software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory.
The software allocations are removed from the asset, but not returned to inventory.
The behavior is controlled by the configurable system property glide.ham.retire_reclaim_sw().
The behavior is controlled by the configurable system property glide.ham.retire_sw().

questions.explanation: When a hardware asset like a server is retired, software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory (B). This is the expected behavior in the HAM+SAM integrated environment. Note: Community consensus is low (44%) and Q166 reflects a different community perspective on this question.

questions.stem: With regard to Contract Management notifications, what is the most important contract dale to be aware of?
questions.explanation: The most important contract date to be aware of for notifications is the Expire date (C). Contract administrators are notified 90, 60, and 30 days before and on the expiration date, making timely action critical to avoid penalties or service disruptions.

questions.stem: Inventory audit results provide easy visibility into the reconciliation of scanned assets to the existing inventory. What audit statuses are displayed as part of the results? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four audit statuses displayed are New (C - scanned but not in CMDB), Scanned and not expected (D - found but not at expected location), Scanned and expected (E - found and confirmed), and Expected and not found (F - expected but physically missing).

questions.stem: How can you automate the replenishment of stock levels?
questions.explanation: Stock rules (D) automate the replenishment of stock levels by triggering purchase orders or transfer orders when inventory falls below a specified threshold. Stock rules define the conditions and actions for automatic restocking.

questions.stem: What are baseline asset states? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline asset states include In Stock (A), Consumed (B), and Retired (C). These are standard states in the asset lifecycle in ServiceNow ITAM. Duplicate (D) and Exported (E) are not standard asset state values.

questions.stem: What field must an agent complete when resolving an incident in order for the HAM asset tasks to automatically update all configuration item (CI) and asset records associated to the Incident?
questions.explanation: When resolving an incident, the agent must complete the Asset Action (D) field to trigger HAM asset tasks that automatically update all associated CI and asset records. This field specifies what action to take on the assets affected by the incident.

questions.stem: Which mobile app allows the user to conduct an inventory audit?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Agent mobile app (A) allows users to conduct inventory audits by scanning asset barcodes at stockrooms and locations. The the docs confirms the Agent app is required for asset audit scanning functionality.

questions.stem: When running an asset audit, you receive the result of 10 "Scanned and expected" assets. What does this mean?

options.text: You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned 10 assets during your audit, but none of them are on your expected inventory list.
You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned these 10 assets during your audit.
You expected 10 assets during your audit inventory and scanned 10 assets, but none of them have a record in your ServiceNow instance.
You scanned 10 assets in your inventory, but none of them were on your expected inventory list.

questions.explanation: A result of 10 'Scanned and expected' means you expected 10 assets at that location AND physically scanned those same 10 assets during the audit (B). These assets are confirmed to be exactly where they should be in the inventory.

questions.stem: During an audit, when is the Expected Assets list populated in the asset audit form?

options.text: When the nightly scheduled job runs
Pre-populated by the asset manager before audit
When the asset manager Submits the results

questions.explanation: The Expected Assets list in the audit form is populated when scanning begins — specifically when you scan an asset for the first time in the audit (C). The the docs states: 'This list gets populated when you scan an asset for the first time in the audit.'

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid substates of the Retired state? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Valid substates of the Retired state are Disposed (A), Donated (B), Pending Disposal (E), and Sold (F). The the docs explicitly lists these four: 'Disposed, Pending disposal, Sold, Donated.' Vendor Credit (C) and Destroyed (D) are not documented Retired substates.

questions.stem:
When a stock manager receives a new delivery of consumables, what happens if all the following fields match another record in the stockroom?
• Assigned to
• Model
• Model category
• State
• Stockroom
• Substate

options.text: The stock manager must create a separate model record if the cost per item is more/less
The data is automatically merged to create a blended quantity and cost
The data is automatically created in a new record if the cost per item is more/less
The stock manager must merge the consumable records to create a blended quantity and cost

questions.explanation: When all key fields match (assigned to, model, model category, state, stockroom, substate), newly received consumables are automatically merged to create a blended quantity and weighted average cost (B). Similar records consolidate automatically when no conflicting data exists.

questions.stem: How does an end user determine what consumables they have consumed?

options.text: Navigate to Asset > Hardware Asset Dashboard
Navigate to Self-Service > My Hardware Asset Dashboard

questions.explanation: End users determine what consumables they have consumed by navigating to Self-Service > My Assets (B). This module shows all assets and consumables assigned to or consumed by the user. 'My Consumables' is not a separate module.

questions.stem: When using transfer orders to move multiple assets from a single stockroom to another, how should each asset be listed?

options.text: Each asset should be listed as a transfer order line on the transfer order
Each asset should be listed in a transfer order task on the transfer order
Each asset should be listed as a transfer order line on the transfer order task
Each asset should be listed in an individual transfer order

questions.explanation: When transferring multiple assets from one stockroom to another, each asset is listed as a transfer order line on the transfer order (A). The the docs shows adding assets via 'New' under Transfer Order Lines on the transfer order record.

questions.stem: What happens to the associated assets when you cancel a transfer order line on a transfer order?

options.text: The asset(s) on the order line are released, but their state remains Pre-allocated
The asset(s) on the order line are released and they can be attached to another transfer order
All assets on the transfer order are released, but their state remains Pre-allocated
A transfer order line cannot be cancelled once it is in a state of Ready for fulfillment
All assets on the transfer order are released and they can be attached to another transfer order

questions.explanation: When a transfer order line is cancelled, the assets on that order line are released and can be attached to another transfer order (B). The business rule 'Release Asset on TOL cancel/delete' places the corresponding asset back into stock. Only that TOL's assets are released, not all assets on the transfer order.

questions.stem: When transferring non-consumable assets between stockrooms, how must they be transferred?

options.text: No more than 10% of the source stockroom's inventory
As a single entity with a quantity of one

questions.explanation: Non-consumable assets must be transferred as a single entity with a quantity of one (C). Consumable assets can be transferred with quantity greater than one. This ensures accurate individual asset tracking during stockroom transfers.

questions.stem: When disposing of an IT asset through a vendor, what documentation should be attached to the retired asset's record as proof of adherence to environmental, regulatory, and legal requirements?
questions.explanation: When disposing of an IT asset through a vendor, a Certificate of Disposal (D) should be attached to the retired asset record as proof of adherence to environmental, regulatory, and legal requirements. This documents the compliant end-of-life process.

questions.stem: You may adjust a contract when it is in which of the following states? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A contract can be adjusted when it is in Active (A) or Expired (D) states. The 'Adjust' function allows modifying contract start date, end date, and payment amount. Canceled, Extended, and Renewed states do not support the adjustment workflow.

questions.stem: Which catalogs support the request and procurement process? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three catalogs supporting the request and procurement process are the Product Catalog (A - model repository), Vendor Catalog (B - links models to vendor items for purchasing), and Service Catalog (D - where users request assets). Asset Catalog and Procurement Catalog are not standard ServiceNow catalog types.

questions.stem: What are the three types of catalogs in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three types of catalogs in ServiceNow are the Product Catalog (A), Vendor Catalog (D), and Service Catalog (E). These cover model management, vendor sourcing, and end-user requesting respectively. Consumable Catalog and Asset Catalog are not distinct catalog types.

questions.stem: The Stock Rule Runner scheduled job replenishes stock in a stockroom__________.

options.text: When stock is less than the threshold specified in the stock rule
By creating a purchase orders to restock from other stockrooms
By creating transfer orders to restock from other stockrooms
By notifying the stockroom manager of new transfer orders

questions.explanation: The Stock Rule Runner scheduled job replenishes stock when stock is less than the threshold specified in the stock rule (A). When triggered, it creates a purchase order (if Procurement is active) or a task for the stockroom manager.

questions.stem: When creating a list report that groups all assets by product model, which table is used?
questions.explanation: When creating a list report that groups all assets by product model, the Asset table [alm_asset] (A) is used. This table contains all asset records including their model references, allowing grouping by product model. The the docs lists alm_asset as the source table for asset reports.

questions.stem: Assets can be scanned and created in ServiceNow via the Agent mobile application in which scenarios? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a single asset via barcode scan
Receive one or multiple assets from a purchase order
Create multiple assets listed on a contract PDF scan
Create a single asset via Name search

questions.explanation: Assets can be scanned and created via the ServiceNow Agent mobile app by creating a single asset via barcode scan (A) or receiving one or multiple assets from a purchase order (B). The the docs confirms barcode scanning for single and multiple PO receipts. Contract PDF scanning and name search are not supported scenarios.

questions.stem: When viewing the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard, you see that several models are reported as Match Not Found. What are potential causes of this? (Choose three.)

options.text: You have opted out of the Content Service
The content is not available from the Content Service
Your model form contains a good Model number, but a bad model Name
Something on your model form may be badly formatted
The content has not been downloaded from the Content Service

questions.explanation: 'Match Not Found' on the Model Management tab indicates the normalization lookup failed. Causes include: content not available from the Content Service (B), badly formatted model form data (D), and content not yet downloaded from the Content Service (E). Opting out (A) affects data sharing, not match results.

questions.stem: Which of the following are components of the asset request structure? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Components of the asset request structure are Transfer orders (B), Purchase orders (D), and Catalog tasks (E). The the docs confirms that a catalog task is auto-generated for each requested item, which may result in a purchase order or transfer order. 'Procurement orders' and 'Stock order tasks' are not standard terms.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of the Inventory tab of the Hardware Asset Management dashboard?

options.text: Help the asset manager generate reports
Show the value from maintaining inventory
Help the stock manager process transfer orders
Show the value from bulk purchasing
Help the asset manager process purchase orders

questions.explanation: The primary goal of the Inventory tab of the Hardware Asset Management dashboard is to show the value from maintaining inventory (B). It displays stock levels, inventory compliance, and inventory metrics that demonstrate the business value of proper inventory management.

questions.stem: What do certification filters define?

options.text: The percentage of tasks required for the certification to be considered complete
What fields are displayed for certification

questions.explanation: Certification filters define the assets to be certified (C) - they determine which asset records are included in the inventory audit/certification scope. This is separate from certification schedules (when) and task configurations (fields displayed).

questions.stem: Which features are part of the ServiceNow Mobile App? (Choose two.)

options.text: Provides end users visibility to their assigned hardware
Provides users visibility to their disposed consumables
Enables end users to log incidents for their assigned assets

questions.explanation: ServiceNow Mobile App features for HAM include providing end users visibility to their assigned hardware (A) and enabling end users to log incidents for their assigned assets (D). Mobile device reclamation (B) is a SAM feature; viewing disposed consumables (C) is not a standard mobile feature.

questions.stem: What information would you find on the End of Life tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: New hardware assets found by audits
Consumable models up for End of Life

questions.explanation: The End of Life tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard shows hardware asset disposal status (A) and hardware assets disposed year-to-date (C). The the docs -1171 confirms the tab monitors assets approaching end of life and disposal status including YTD disposal counts.

questions.stem: What are some examples of operational expenses of managing an asset throughout its lifecycle? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Operational expenses during an asset's lifecycle include replacement parts (A) for repairs/maintenance and maintenance agreements (C) for ongoing support contracts. Storage costs (B) are capital/logistical; warranty costs (D) are typically bundled in the purchase price, not separate operational expenses.

questions.stem: What is the name of the scheduled job that generates expense lines based on rate cards?
questions.explanation: The scheduled job that generates expense lines based on rate cards is 'Process FM Costs' (B). It runs on the Contract table once per day, running forward and backward to generate expense lines based on rate card costs incurred during the contract period.

questions.stem: How do you calculate residual value?

options.text: Subtract the amortized value from the cost of the asset
Subtract storage and lease cost from the cost of the asset
Subtract the depreciation from the cost of the asset
Subtract the salvage value from the cost of the asset

questions.explanation: Residual value is calculated by subtracting the accumulated depreciation from the original cost of the asset (C). The formula is: Residual Value = Purchase Cost - Accumulated Depreciation. The salvage value is the estimated value at end of useful life, not a subtractor for residual value.

questions.stem: Configuration items (CIs) track what type of information? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Configuration items (CIs) track Operational information (B - how the device is configured and functioning) and Relationship information (E - connections to other CIs and business services). Financial, lifecycle, and contractual data belong in the Asset Management records.

questions.stem: When does an asset’s lifecycle begin?

options.text: When an asset request is fulfilled

questions.explanation: An asset's lifecycle begins upon the asset's request (D). The request is the first stage, initiating the full lifecycle: Request → Procure → Receive → Deploy → Monitor → Service → Retire. The lifecycle is formally started when someone requests the asset.

questions.stem: What are the goals of IT asset management (ITAM)? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four goals of IT asset management are Optimize cost (A), Provide decision support (B), Improve productivity (C), and Provide financial reporting (D). These represent the core value drivers of ITAM. Operational usage optimization and logical relationship tracking are CMDB/operational management concerns.

questions.stem: A given collection of methodologies, assets, and templates within Now Create is referred to as what?
questions.explanation: A collection of methodologies, assets, and templates within Now Create is referred to as a Success pack (C). Success packs provide structured guidance and templates for implementing ServiceNow capabilities.

questions.stem: To access the full spectrum of asset management functionality, which inactive plugins should be installed? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: The five inactive plugins needed for full asset management functionality are Cost Management (B), Procurement (C), Hardware Asset Management (D), Data Certification (E), and Managed Documents (G). Discovery (A) and Service Mapping (F) are separate platform capabilities not specific to ITAM.

questions.stem: What are the four tiers of Capability Blueprint?

options.text: Trustworthy Data, Lifecycle Management, Process Integration, Strategic Conformance
Trustworthy Data, Practical Management, Process Integration, Business Alignment
Trustworthy Data, Practical Management, Operational Integration, Strategic Conformance
Trustworthy Data, Lifecycle Management, Operational integration, Business Alignment

questions.explanation: The four tiers of the Capability Blueprint are Trustworthy Data (Tier 1), Practical Management (Tier 2), Operational Integration (Tier 3), and Strategic Conformance (Tier 4). This represents the ITAM maturity progression from data quality through strategic business alignment.

questions.stem: What core table requires migration when extending ITSM Asset Management with Hardware Asset Management?
questions.explanation: No migration is required (C) when extending ITSM Asset Management with Hardware Asset Management. HAM extends the existing ITSM asset tables and infrastructure without requiring data migration of the existing asset or model records.

questions.stem: How could you quickly determine if you had the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) plugin installed on your instance?

options.text: Check for the Hardware Assets module in the application navigator
Check for the Hardware Asset Dashboard module in the application navigator
Check for the Asset application in the application navigator
Check for the Hardware Asset Management application in the application navigator

questions.explanation: To quickly determine if HAM is installed, check for the Hardware Asset Dashboard module (B) in the application navigator. This dashboard is exclusively added by the HAM plugin and is not present in baseline ITSM Asset Management.

questions.stem: A component is considered an IT asset when you want to: (Choose three.)

options.text: Know its relationships to a business service

questions.explanation: A component is considered an IT asset when you want to manage its procurement (A), track its incurred costs (D), or manage its maintenance contracts (E). Knowing business service relationships (B) and tracking operational information (C) define CI management purposes.

questions.stem: Which is NOT considered an asset?
questions.explanation: Websites (A) are digital services/properties and are NOT considered assets in ServiceNow ITAM. Switches and routers (hardware), buildings (facilities), and software entitlements are all standard asset types tracked in the Asset Management application.

questions.stem: What are model records?

options.text: Models are specific versions or various configurations of an asset
Models are any computer, device, software or service in the CMDB
Models directly associate configuration item (CI) classes with asset classes
Models are anything capable of being owned or controlled to produce economic value

questions.explanation: Model records are specific versions or various configurations of an asset (A). They serve as templates in the product catalog defining the type of asset, and asset records reference a model. The the docs confirms this definition.

questions.stem: Which of the following are functions of the model category? (Choose two.)

options.text: Model categories group consumables in the Product Catalog
Model categories determine when to create assets from configuration items (Cls)
Model categories group related assets in the Service Catalog
Model categories provide the link between configuration management and asset management
Model categories provide the link between procurement management and asset management

questions.explanation: Model categories serve two functions: determining when to create assets from configuration items (B - via the asset tracking strategy field), and providing the link between configuration management and asset management (D - by connecting CI classes to asset classes).

questions.stem: When does hardware normalization run by default?
questions.explanation: Hardware normalization runs daily (B) by default. The the docs confirms: 'The HAM-Hardware Normalization scheduled job runs daily.' It only updates normalization-related fields and does not modify original fields like Model Name or Manufacturer.

questions.stem: For a model to be fully normalized, what must be added to the model record?
questions.explanation: For a model to be fully normalized, the Model number (D) must be added to the model record. The the docs states: 'For a model to be fully normalized, you must add manufacturer details and a [model number].' Without model number, the status remains Partially Normalized.

questions.stem: Which elements are provided by the hardware asset management content service? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The HAM content service provides Manufacturer lifecycle dates (A - EoL/EoS dates), normalized Manufacturer data (D - standardized names), and Model name data (E). Cost (B) is purchase/financial data. Product warranty (C) and Compatibles (F) are not standard content service outputs.

questions.stem: What hardware asset attribute should you track that is NOT part of a configuration item (CI)?
questions.explanation: Cost (C) is a hardware asset attribute that is NOT part of a CI. Cost is financial data tracked in the Asset Management application. IP address, CPU, operating system, and memory are all operational/technical attributes tracked in the CMDB as CI data.

questions.stem: Under which condition does the Now Platform NOT create an asset automatically?
questions.explanation: The Now Platform does NOT create an asset automatically when Enforced CI verification (B) is selected on the model category form. The the docs confirms this: 'Forced CI verification: If you select the Enforce CI verification option, the platform does not create an asset automatically.'

questions.stem: Which three attributes from a hardware model record are used for setting the normalized display name during hardware model normalization?

options.text: Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model number
Name, Asset tracking unit, Model number
Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model category

questions.explanation: The three attributes used to set the normalized display name during hardware model normalization are Name, Manufacturer, and Model number (C). The display name is generated from these three fields on the hardware model record.

questions.stem: Which key attribute in the model record does hardware model normalization use to normalize inconsistent manufactures and product names?
questions.explanation: The Model number (D) is the key attribute that hardware model normalization uses to normalize inconsistent manufacturer and product names. The model number uniquely identifies the specific product configuration in the Content Service library.

questions.stem: What plugin offers consistent, good, clean data for the company names of vendors or manufactures?
questions.explanation: The Normalization Data Services Client plugin (com.glide.data_services_canonicalization.client) (D) provides consistent, clean data for company names of vendors and manufacturers. It powers the central normalization engine that standardizes company name data across the platform.

questions.stem: Hardware models may not be fully normalized until updated content is downloaded from the Hardware Model Normalization Content Service. How do you determine if the content has been downloaded?

options.text: Determine if the business rule, Create a Hardware Normalization Download, has been triggered yet or not
Review the Last updated date of the Central Data Service Download Status jobs on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard
Review the Hardware Model Content Service Download section on the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard
Query the scheduled job reports to determine if the Hardware Normalization Content Library Download job has completed yet

questions.explanation: To determine if content has been downloaded from the Hardware Model Normalization Content Service, review the Hardware Model Content Service Download section on the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard (C). This section shows the download status and last updated date.

questions.stem: How do you prevent normalization information fora specific hardware model from being sent to the ServiceNow Content Service?

options.text: Select Exclude from content service on the Normalization tab of the hardware model record
Click the Exclude button on the hardware model record
Click the Opt-out button on the hardware model record
Select Opt-out from content service on the Normalization tab of the hardware model record

questions.explanation: To prevent normalization information for a specific hardware model from being sent to the Content Service, select 'Exclude from content service' on the Normalization tab of the hardware model record (A). The the docs confirms toggling the exclude option on individual model records.

questions.stem: What are the two primary benefits of deploying asset tasks during the retirement of an asset? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two primary benefits of deploying asset tasks during retirement are reducing manual intervention (A) by automating state changes and data updates, and increasing data accuracy (C) by auto-updating the CI/asset record upon task completion. The the docs confirms tasks automatically update records.

questions.stem: A user’s broken laptop is replaced via an incident. Upon completion, the Incident Management application triggers the swap/replace asset task. Which fields are automatically updated in the associated asset record? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When the swap/replace asset task is triggered via an incident, fields automatically updated in the asset record include software allocations (A), maintenance contracts (B), and the related CI record (D). Depreciation values (C) and disposal information (E) are not auto-updated during a swap.

questions.stem: A transfer order is used to do what?

options.text: Move an asset to an external stockroom
Transfer an asset to a user

questions.explanation: A transfer order is used to move assets between company stockrooms (C). The the docs states: 'Transfer orders move assets between company stockrooms.' They do not transfer to vendors, external stockrooms, or directly to users.

questions.stem: What types of inventory audits are supported with the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) application? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two types of inventory audits supported by HAM are stockroom audits (A) and location audits (C) such as offices or datacenters. The the docs confirms: 'Perform scheduled or blind audits of asset stockrooms and other locations.' Vendor and discovery audits are not HAM audit types.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid contract states? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid contract states are Draft (A), Active (B), and Expired (E). The the docs explicitly defines these three as primary contract states along with Canceled and Renewed. 'In use' and 'New' are not contract states in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: Stockroom C has seven Bluetooth keyboards with a total value of $630. The asset manager procures two more of the same model keyboards for $360 and adds them to Stockroom C. When one of these keyboards is consumed, what is the value of the consumed Bluetooth keyboard?
questions.explanation: Consumables use weighted average costing. Original: 7 keyboards at $630 ($90 each). Procurement: 2 keyboards at $360 ($180 each). Total: 9 keyboards, $990 total. Weighted average = $990/9 = $110. The consumed keyboard has a value of $110 (A).

questions.stem: Which applications are required to perform a blind audit of your asset inventory?

options.text: Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and ServiceNow My Assets mobile app
Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and Software Asset Management (SAM)
ITSM Asset Management and ServiceNow My Assets mobile app
ITSM Asset Management and ServiceNow Agent mobile app
Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and ServiceNow Agent mobile app

questions.explanation: A blind audit requires Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and ServiceNow Agent mobile app (E). The the docs confirms 'Before you begin: Hardware Asset Management, ServiceNow Agent app.' The Agent app is used to scan asset barcodes during the physical audit.

questions.stem: Within the asset audit form, where would you find the list of all assets that were found at the stockroom or warehouse that is being audited?
questions.explanation: The 'Scanned Assets' section (B) of the asset audit form shows the list of all assets found (physically scanned) at the stockroom or location being audited. The the docs confirms: 'Scanned Assets: Shows a list of all assets that are scanned during the audit.'

questions.stem: What is the purpose of stock rules? (Choose two.)

options.text: To automatically transfer assets when a low quantity threshold is detected in a stockroom
To track stock orders from a vendor
To send notifications when a low quantity threshold is detected in a stockroom
To track stock movement between stockrooms
To send notifications when a stock shipment arrives at a stockroom

questions.explanation: Stock rules serve two purposes: automatically transferring inventory when low quantity threshold is detected in a stockroom (A), and sending notifications when a low quantity threshold is detected (C). The the docs confirms stock rules 'can either notify an asset manager or automatically transfer inventory.'

questions.stem: Which of an organization’s assets are managed using stockrooms?

options.text: All available stock, consumable or not

questions.explanation: All available stock is managed using stockrooms — both consumable and non-consumable assets (A). Stockrooms are the centralized locations for receiving, storing, and distributing all types of hardware assets. Only managing consumables (B) would be incorrect.

questions.stem: When using transform maps to transform imported hardware model data to your desired asset tables, what option do you set to uniquely identify the same asset in order to merge/update records?
questions.explanation: The 'Coalesce' option (A) in transform maps uniquely identifies the same asset to merge or update records during import. A coalesced field acts as the unique key to match incoming records against existing records and perform update operations instead of inserts.

questions.stem: An event runs each night to send reminders to contract administrators about contract expiration dates (e.g., so they can renew or renegotiate the contract). By default, when does the contract administrator receive these notifications? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Contract administrators receive expiration notifications by default at 90 days before (E), 60 days before (C), 30 days before (F), and on the day of expiration (D). The the docs confirms: 'notified 90, 60, and 30 days before the expiration date.'

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid contract states during a contract’s lifecycle? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Valid primary contract states documented in ServiceNow are Draft (A), Canceled (B), Active (E), and Expired (G). The the docs explicitly defines these as primary states. Renewed and Extended are management states; Renegotiated is not a documented contract state.

questions.stem: What are the key steps for importing asset data? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three key steps for importing asset data are: Load data (E - import data into the staging table), Create transform map (D - configure field mappings and coalesce keys), and Run transform map (B - execute the transformation to populate target tables). Merge, Update, and Consolidate are not standard import steps.

questions.stem: What must exist before a consumable can be consumed? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Before a consumable can be consumed, three records must exist: a model record (B - defining the consumable type), a model category record (D - the Consumable category), and a consumable asset record (E - the actual consumable instance). The the docs confirms model and model category are required first steps.

questions.stem: When using the HAM application, what happens when you create a new transfer order line on a transfer order?

options.text: The asset(s) listed in the transfer order line are automatically transferred to the new stockroom
The transfer order line is automatically placed in a state of Ready for fulfilment
A transfer order line task is automatically created to move the transfer order line from one stage to another
A transfer order line task is automatically created to validate enough stock exists
The asset(s) listed in the transfer order line are automatically readied for shipment

questions.explanation: When you create a new transfer order line, a transfer order line task is automatically created to move the TOL from one stage to the next (C). The the docs confirms 'a transfer order line task is automatically created' based on the model category of the asset.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow Mobile app provides end users visibility to their assigned hardware and consumable assets?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Mobile App (B) provides end users visibility to their assigned hardware and consumable assets. This is distinct from the ServiceNow Agent app which is used by inventory/asset managers for operations like receiving assets and performing audits.

questions.stem: Select the three main components of the data certification process. (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three main components of the data certification process are Create the certification filter (C - defines which assets to certify), Create the certification schedule (D - defines when certification runs), and Run the certification (E - executes the audit/verification process). 'Certify the certification' and 'Assign tasks' are not primary components.

questions.stem: Which catalog facilitates the ability to source from existing stock?
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog (C) facilitates sourcing from existing stock. When users submit a request via Service Catalog, the Source Request flow triggers catalog tasks that can fulfill requests from local stockrooms. The Procurement Catalog and Vendor Catalog facilitate purchasing from external vendors. Product Catalog (D) is where hardware models are managed.

questions.stem: From where can you publish catalog items? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Catalog items can be published from a model (E) using the 'Publish to Hardware Catalog' related link on the product model record, or from a vendor item (D) via the Vendor Catalog Item form. Model categories (A), asset records (B), and user records (C) do not have publish-to-catalog functionality.

questions.stem: Publishing an item to the Service Catalog can be done by using the “Publish to Hardware Catalog” related link in:
questions.explanation: The 'Publish to Hardware Catalog' related link is located on product model records in the Product Catalog (A). Navigate to All > Product Catalog > Product Model > All Models, open a model, and use Related Links to publish to the hardware catalog. The link does not appear in Inventory, Asset, or Supplier catalogs.

questions.stem: An asset is manually created from a purchase order before it has been shipped by the supplier. By default, the state of the asset is set to:
questions.explanation: When an asset is manually created from a purchase order before the supplier has shipped it, the default asset state is On order (A). This reflects the asset's early lifecycle position — ordered but not yet received or deployed. In use (B), Awaiting delivery (C), and Pending transfer (D) represent different lifecycle stages.

questions.stem: How often are the tabs in the Hardware Asset dashboard updated?
questions.explanation: The tabs in the Hardware Asset dashboard are updated in real time (C). The dashboard leverages Performance Analytics to provide live metrics on hardware and consumable models and assets across the full asset lifecycle. Daily (A), hourly (B), and 15-minute (D) intervals are not the update frequency for dashboard tabs.

questions.stem: What minimum role is required in order to use the Hardware Asset dashboard?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to use the Hardware Asset dashboard is the asset role (A). The doc confirms that asset, itil, contract_manager, inventory_admin, or ham_admin can access the dashboard — making asset the minimum. ham_user (C) and ham_admin (D) are higher or non-standard roles for this purpose.

questions.stem: What information would you find on the Inventory tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose three.)

options.text: New hardware assets found by audits
Hardware models up for end of life

questions.explanation: The Inventory tab shows: New hardware assets found by audits (A), Active stock rules (D), and Open asset audits (E). Hardware models up for end of life (B) and hardware nearing end of warranty (C) appear on the End of Life tab. Requests requiring sourcing (F) appear in procurement views.

questions.stem: Which mobile app can users leverage to create assets, perform inventory audits, and receive assets?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Agent app (A) allows users to create assets, look up assets, perform inventory audits, and receive assets from purchase orders. The the docs explicitly lists these capabilities. Now Mobile (C) is for end users; Now Procurement (B) and Now Onboarding (D) are not the correct apps for these HAM functions.

questions.stem: Several of your models are listed as Match Not Found on the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard. What are the potential causes of this? (Choose three.)

options.text: The hardware model content has not yet been downloaded from the Content Service
Normalization could not match any of the three key fields in the hardware model form with a rule in the Content Service
Your hardware model form contains a good model number, but a badly formatted model name
You have opted out of the ServiceNow Content Service
A normalization rule for the hardware model does not exist in the Content Service

questions.explanation: Three causes are: hardware model content not yet downloaded from Content Service (A), normalization could not match any of the three key fields with a Content Service rule (B), and no normalization rule exists in the Content Service for the model (E). A valid model number overrides a bad name so C is wrong. Opting out (D) prevents normalization entirely.

questions.stem: What original costs are involved in purchasing an asset and putting it into use? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Original costs involved in acquiring and putting an asset into use include Lease costs (A), Delivery costs (B - shipping/transport), and Storage costs (E - pre-deployment storage). Spare parts (C) and Maintenance (D) are ongoing operational costs incurred during use, not original acquisition costs.

questions.stem: A scheduled job runs nightly to determine if any rate cards need to be applied to generate expense lines. What is the name of the scheduled job?
questions.explanation: The scheduled job 'Process FM Costs' (C) runs on the Contract table once per day to determine if rate cards need to be applied and generate expense lines. The the docs confirms: 'The scheduled job, Process FM Costs, runs on the Contract [ast_contract] table once per day.' Other names (A, B, D) do not exist as scheduled jobs.

questions.stem: What is included in the total cost of ownership? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) includes Original cost (B - initial capital acquisition cost) and Operational expense (D - ongoing expense lines from rate cards and maintenance). The the docs states TCO is calculated by adding all expense lines to the initial capital cost. Delivery cost (A) is part of original cost; Depreciation (C) is not tracked as an expense line in ServiceNow TCO.

questions.stem: What is a requirement for sourcing a request from the requester’s local stockroom?

options.text: The requested stock must be in transit from a vendor
The requested stock must be available in the local stockroom
The requested stock must be available via transfer order from a remote stockroom
The requested stock must be in transit from a remote stockroom

questions.explanation: The requirement for sourcing from the requester's local stockroom is that stock must be available in the local stockroom (B). The the docs confirms: 'You can source a request by using assets from the requester's local stockroom, if stock is available in the local stockroom.' If unavailable, assets transfer from other stockrooms or a PO is created.

questions.stem: By default, what Quick links are available on the Hardware asset overview view? (Choose three.)

options.text: Assets eligible for refresh by model category

questions.explanation: The three default Quick links on the Hardware asset overview are Transfer orders (A), Asset requests (C), and Model normalization (D). The the docs lists these as navigation links to key asset function dashboards. Assets eligible for refresh (B), Asset count by model category (E), and Asset count by lifecycle state (F) appear in the 360 asset view section.

questions.stem: A component is considered a configuration item (CI) as opposed to an IT asset when you want to:
questions.explanation: A component is considered a CI rather than an IT asset when you want to track its relationship information (C) — connections to other CIs and business services. Tracking incurred costs (A), managing retirement (B), managing license contracts (D), and knowing who uses it (E) are asset management purposes. Relationship tracking defines CI management in the CMDB.

questions.stem: What is tracked throughout the life of an asset? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three types of data tracked throughout the life of an asset are Financial data (A - purchase price, TCO), Contractual data (B - maintenance and lease contracts), and Lifecycle data (C - state transitions). Configuration data (D) is tracked in the CMDB for CIs. Hardware data (E) refers to technical specs managed as CI attributes, not core asset data.

questions.stem: What is the focus of asset management?

options.text: Financial tracking of an organization's property
Financial tracking of the organization's network
Building the elements that create the organization's network

questions.explanation: The focus of asset management is financial tracking of an organization's property (A). ITAM tracks procurement costs, TCO, contracts, and depreciation of organizational assets. Building the elements of the network (D) describes infrastructure deployment/configuration management, not asset management. Note: Community says D (100%) but standard ITAM definition supports A.

questions.stem: Which tier of the capability blueprint focuses on achieving best-in-class?
questions.explanation: Strategic Conformance (C) is the fourth and highest tier of the ITAM Capability Blueprint, representing best-in-class practices. Tiers progress: Tier 1 (Trustworthy Data) → Tier 2 (Practical Management) → Tier 3 (Operational Integration) → Tier 4 (Strategic Conformance). Achieving best-in-class means full business alignment at Tier 4.

questions.stem: Which of the following are components of the ServiceNow asset lifecycle? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Three components of the ServiceNow asset lifecycle are Procure (C), Request (D), and Receive (F). The full lifecycle sequence is: Request → Procure → Receive → Deploy → Monitor → Service → Retire. Discard (A) is not a lifecycle stage name; Order (B) is not a named stage; Install (E) is not a formal ServiceNow asset lifecycle phase.

questions.stem: What are the five valid phases of the Now Create methodology?
questions.explanation: The five valid phases of the Now Create methodology are Initiate, Plan, Execute, Deliver, and Close (B). This is the standard project delivery framework embedded in ServiceNow's Now Create for implementing ServiceNow solutions. Review (A, C) and recap (A, C) are not valid Now Create phase names.

questions.stem: What are types of assets? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four types of assets are Software entitlement (B), Hardware (C), Consumable (D), and Facility (F). A Model (A) is a template in the product catalog, not an asset. A Stockroom (E) is a physical location for storing assets, not an asset type itself.

questions.stem: What are the baseline asset lifecycle automation flows provided by the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) plugin? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three baseline asset lifecycle automation flows provided by the HAM plugin are Hardware asset order (A), Hardware bulk stock order (B), and Hardware disposal (F). These cover procurement initiation, bulk purchasing, and end-of-life disposal workflows.

questions.stem: What plugin helps alleviate inconsistencies in company names?
questions.explanation: The Normalization Data Services plugin alleviates inconsistencies in company names by providing a centralized normalization engine that standardizes manufacturer, vendor, and company name data across the platform.

questions.stem: What are the Normalization statuses? (Choose six.)
questions.explanation: The six normalization statuses are Manufacturer Normalized (A), Match Not Found (B), Partially Normalized (C), Normalized (D), Manually Normalized (E), and New (G). The the docs and confirm these. Version Normalized (F) and Found (H) are not valid statuses.

questions.stem: An asset record tracks which data that is NOT part of configuration management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Asset records track data NOT part of configuration management: Lifecycle data (A), Contractual data (B), and Financial data (C). The Asset table [alm_asset] stores 'general, financial, and contractual information.' Operational (E) and Logical (D) data belongs in configuration management.

questions.stem: When selected on the model category form, what feature prevents the automatic creation of an asset?
questions.explanation: Selecting 'Enforce CI Verification' (E) on the model category form prevents the system from automatically creating an asset when a CI is added in that category. The the docs confirms this prevents automatic asset creation, requiring manual review.

questions.stem: In order for a hardware model to be fully normalized rather than partially normalized, what field is required in the hardware model record?
questions.explanation: For a hardware model to be fully normalized (not partially), the Model number (E) field is required. The the docs confirms: 'For a model to be fully normalized, you must add manufacturer details and a [model number].' Partially normalized uses only manufacturer + product name.

questions.stem: You have just created a new hardware model record for a group of laptops you purchased. When does normalization first run to normalize the record?

options.text: When the daily scheduled HAM – Daily job runs
When the weekly scheduled HAM – Normalization job runs
When you save the hardware model record
When you click the Normalize Hardware Model link under Related Links

questions.explanation: Normalization first runs when you save the hardware model record (C). The daily scheduled job normalizes existing records, but saving a new record triggers immediate normalization against the Content Service.

questions.stem: When opted-in to the Hardware Asset Management Content Service, how often is updated content downloaded to the customer instance from ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: When opted in to the HAM Content Service, updated content is downloaded to the customer instance daily (C). The HAM-Hardware Normalization scheduled job runs daily to update normalization-related fields with the latest content.

questions.stem: Normalization status is the level of normalization match based on what characteristics? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Normalization status is determined by the level of match on three characteristics: Model name (A), Model number (C), and Manufacturer (E). Full normalization requires all three; partial normalization has manufacturer + product name only; manufacturer normalized has only manufacturer.

questions.stem: As part of the hardware model normalization process, the Content Library automatically populates your inventory with what non-discoverable asset metadata?
questions.explanation: As part of hardware model normalization, the Content Library automatically populates manufacturer lifecycle dates (C) - such as General Availability, End of Sale, End of Support, and End of Life dates. These dates are non-discoverable and can only be sourced from the manufacturer content service.

questions.stem: What core sets of data are required for effective IT asset management? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four core data sets required for effective IT asset management are Manufacturers (A - for normalization), Locations (C - where assets are deployed), Users (D - who assets are assigned to), and Models (F - defining asset types and specs). Relationships and Projects are supplemental data.

questions.stem: What role is required to use the Hardware Model Normalization Overview dashboard?
questions.explanation: The asset role (E) is required to use the Hardware Model Normalization Overview dashboard. The asset role provides access to asset management dashboards and reports, while ham_admin is for administrative configuration tasks.

questions.stem: When working in conjunction with a Field Service Management (FSM) change task, what feature removes the need to manually update the asset record associated to the task?
questions.explanation: Asset tasks (D) remove the need to manually update the asset record associated with an FSM change task. The the docs confirms: 'If an asset is being deployed, replaced, or retired via a field service work order, the CI/asset record is automatically updated.'

questions.stem: For what asset actions are asset tasks provided? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Asset tasks are provided for Retire (B), Update/Repair (C), and Swap (D) operations. The the docs describes asset tasks for 'deploy, replace or swap, or retirement operations.' Community consensus at 71% maps these to retire, update/repair, and swap actions.

questions.stem: What happens to the consumable's asset record after it has been consumed?

options.text: The record is marked inactive but remains in the system
The record state is set to In use
The record remains in the system for reporting purposes only
The record is removed from the system

questions.explanation: After a consumable has been consumed, the asset record remains in the system for reporting purposes only (C). The the docs explicitly states: 'After a consumable is consumed, the record remains in the system for reporting purposes.'

questions.stem: A contract can be cancelled when the State is what?
questions.explanation: A contract can be cancelled when the State is Active (B). The the docs confirms that after cancellation, 'the contract State changes to Canceled' from Active. Expired contracts can be renewed, not cancelled.

questions.stem: During an inventory audit, what happens if you accidentally scan the same asset twice?

options.text: The most recent scan is imported

questions.explanation: If the same asset is scanned twice during an inventory audit, HAM automatically removes duplicates (C). The Scanned Assets list is updated with each scan submission but deduplicates assets to ensure each appears only once.

questions.stem: A blind inventory audit is typically initiated via which interface?
questions.explanation: A blind inventory audit is typically initiated via the ServiceNow Now Agent Mobile app (C). The the docs confirms that a blind audit requires 'Hardware Asset Management' and the 'ServiceNow Agent app' for scanning assets in the field.

questions.stem: Assets can be moved between stockrooms by using:
questions.explanation: Assets are moved between stockrooms using transfer orders (D). A transfer order is the standard mechanism for moving both consumable and non-consumable assets from one company stockroom to another, with full workflow tracking.

questions.stem: Describe the structure of a Transfer Order.

options.text: Transfer Order > Transfer Order Line > Transfer Order Task
Transfer Order > Transfer Order Task > Transfer Order Line
Transfer Order Task > Transfer Order Line

questions.explanation: A Transfer Order contains Transfer Order Lines, which contain Transfer Order Tasks (B). The hierarchy flows: Transfer Order → Transfer Order Line → Transfer Order Task. Lines represent individual items/models; tasks manage workflow stages. Inverse structures (A, C) and incomplete structure (D) are incorrect.

questions.stem: When running an asset audit, you receive the result of 10 "Expected and not found" assets. What does this mean?

options.text: You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned these 10 assets during your audit.
You scanned 20 assets in your inventory, but only 10 of them were on your expected inventory list.
You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned 10 assets during your audit, but none of them are on your expected inventory list.
You expected 10 assets during your audit inventory and scanned 10 assets, but none of them have a record in your ServiceNow instance.

questions.explanation: Community selects D (100%). Note: 'Expected and not found' typically means assets expected at the location per CMDB but not physically scanned. Option D's wording ('none have a record in ServiceNow') conflicts with standard audit definitions. Low confidence due to option wording inconsistency with audit status definitions established.

questions.stem: What requirements must be met in order for a consumable asset to be consumed? (Choose three.)

options.text: State is In stock or Pending Delivery

questions.explanation: Three requirements for consuming a consumable: Quantity > 0 (A), State is In stock (F), and Substate is Available (D). 'In stock or Pending Delivery' (B) is too broad; Substate pre-allocated (C) prevents general consumption; exceeding threshold (E) triggers stock rules, not consumption eligibility.

questions.stem: What are the main purposes of transfer order line tasks? (Choose two.)

options.text: To help track service levels and the time frame needed to complete a transfer order
To move transfer order lines from one stage to another
To help track the total number of assets moved from one stockroom to another
To automate reordering of consumables as they are consumed by users
To move transfer orders from one stage to another

questions.explanation: Transfer order line tasks serve two purposes: tracking service levels and time frame to complete a transfer (A), and moving transfer order lines from one workflow stage to another (B). They don't track total asset counts (C), automate reordering (D), or directly move the parent transfer order (E).

questions.stem: What prevents two asset managers from transferring the same asset at the same time?
questions.explanation: A business rule (A) prevents two asset managers from adding the same asset to two different transfer orders simultaneously. The the docs explicitly states: 'A business rule prevents the same asset from being transferred on two different transfer orders at the same time.' Stock rules (B) manage replenishment.

questions.stem: When should you retire an IT asset?

options.text: At any point it is recommended by the HAM-defined asset policy
At any point that it is recommended by your company-defined policies and procedures
At any point it is recommended by the HAM-defined asset disposal procedure
When the Hardware Content Service Lifecycle data reports the asset is nearing end-of-service
When the Hardware Content Service Lifecycle data reports the asset is nearing end-of-life

questions.explanation: You should retire an IT asset at any point recommended by your company-defined policies and procedures (B). Retirement timing is governed by organizational policy. HAM-defined procedures (A, C) don't dictate retirement. Content Service lifecycle data (D, E) informs the retirement decision but does not solely trigger it.

questions.stem: What critical information should be tracked for your contracts? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two most critical contract tracking items are what each contract costs (B - financial obligation) and what assets each contract covers (D - coverage scope). Who purchased assets (A) is less relevant to ongoing contract management; what needs cancellation (C) is an action item, not critical tracking data.

questions.stem: Why may users request loaner assets even when the requested asset is not available in the local stockroom?

options.text: The request creates an automatic transfer order to move assets from a warehouse with in stock assets.
The wait-listed loaner asset requests provide visibility to streamline internal transfer order flows.
The wait-listed loaner asset requests provide visibility to the demand for loaner orders.
The request automatically creates a purchase order to obtain the assets from a vendor.

questions.explanation: Users request loaner assets even when unavailable because wait-listed requests provide visibility to the demand for loaner orders (C). The the docs explains that when new assets are added or confirmed orders are canceled, wait-listed orders are confirmed in submission sequence, enabling demand-driven provisioning.

questions.stem: Stock rules have automatic restocking actions that occur through a daily scheduled job. What plugin must be activated in order to configure and use the scheduled job?
questions.explanation: The Procurement plugin (B) must be activated for the stock rule automatic restocking scheduled job. The the docs confirms: when a threshold is breached, 'if Procurement is active, a purchase order and purchase order line item are created.' Without Procurement, only a manual task is created.

questions.stem: Classes are represented as tables in the ServiceNow database. Which is the base asset class?
questions.explanation: The base asset class in ServiceNow is alm_asset (C). All asset types extend from this table: alm_hardware (hardware assets) and alm_consumable (consumables) are child classes. cmdb_asset (A) and cmdb_hardware (D) do not exist as standard tables. The CMDB base class is cmdb_ci, separate from the asset hierarchy.

questions.stem: Which view displays metrics to the user to indicate when they are due for a refresh based on the scheduled retirement of their assets?
questions.explanation: The My Assets view (D) displays metrics showing employees when they are due for a refresh based on scheduled asset retirement dates. Employees can see assigned assets and refresh eligibility. Homepage (A), Home (B), and Overview (C) are not the specific view for employee asset refresh visibility.

questions.stem: Which of these automatic restocking actions are available in baseline? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a task assigned to stock room manager to contact procurement manager
Create a task assigned to the stock room manage to create a purchase order
Create a new asset from any returned inventory
Create a transfer order to restock from another stockroom
Create a transfer order to restock from a vendor

questions.explanation: Two baseline automatic restocking actions are: creating a task assigned to the stockroom manager to create a purchase order (B), and creating a transfer order to restock from another stockroom (D). The the docs confirms these two options. Contacting procurement (A), creating assets from returns (C), and vendor transfer orders (E) are not baseline actions.

questions.stem: When sourcing a requested item from a supplier using the catalog task form to create a purchase order, the catalog item must be available in:
questions.explanation: When sourcing from a supplier via catalog task to create a purchase order, the catalog item must be available in the Vendor Catalog (D). The Vendor Catalog contains items from external suppliers with pricing needed to create purchase orders. The Product Catalog (B) hosts the internal hardware models, not vendor-specific items.

questions.stem: What information would you find on the Procurement tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Hardware models up for end of life
New hardware assets found by audits

questions.explanation: The Procurement tab shows Hardware expenditure by vendor (C - financial spend) and Requests that require sourcing (F - pending procurement). Hardware nearing end of warranty (A) and models up for end of life (D) appear on the End of Life tab. New assets from audits (E) appears on the Inventory tab.

questions.stem: Since trustworthy data is key to good asset management practices, where would you look to determine the number of days until next Content Service download will occur?

options.text: Asset Hardware Model Normalization > Content Service Setup

questions.explanation: To see days until the next Content Service download, check the Hardware Asset Dashboard (E). The the docs confirms 'Days until next hardware content refresh' is a widget in the Model Management view of the Hardware Asset dashboard. Content Service Setup (C) manages opt-in, not the countdown.

questions.stem: Which mobile app can users leverage to view the assets assigned to them and create incidents to report issues with their devices?
questions.explanation: The Now Mobile app (C) is for employees to view assets assigned to them and create incidents to report device issues. The Now Agent app (A) is the IT technician app for creating assets, audits, and receiving. Now Onboarding (B) is for employee onboarding; Now My Assets (D) is not a standard app name.

questions.stem: When creating a stock rule that replenishes from a vender, what is primary requirement for the warehouse stockroom? (Choose two.)

options.text: The stockroom manager must have a valid email address
The stockroom must have an assigned manager
The stockroom must have an assignment group
The stockroom manager must have a valid mobile phone
The stockroom manager must have a valid time zone

questions.explanation: For a vendor stock rule, the warehouse stockroom must have an assigned manager (B) and that manager must have a valid email address (A). The the docs shows a business rule 'Managed Stockroom for Vendor Stock Rule' that validates these requirements. Assignment group (C) and mobile phone (D) are not required.

questions.stem: Which tab on the Hardware Asset Dashboard enables tracking asset models with missing purchase details?
questions.explanation: The Asset Health tab (A) enables tracking asset models with missing purchase details and other data quality issues, including missing PO numbers, model numbers, and manufacturer info. Model Management (C) focuses on normalization; Procurement (B) on expenditures; Inventory (D) on audits; End of Life (E) on lifecycle.

questions.stem: To utilize the contract rate cards features, which plugin is required to be activated?
questions.explanation: The Cost Management plugin (D) must be activated to use contract rate card features. The the docs explicitly states: 'You must activate the Cost Management plugin to use rate cards.' Financial Management (A), Contract Management (B), and Rate Management (C) are not the required plugin.
