questions.stem: The current value of an asset (original cost less the depreciated amount) is known as:
questions.explanation: The current value of an asset (original cost minus depreciated amount) is the Residual value (B). The the docs confirms residual value equals original purchase price when depreciation is 0. Salvage value (D) is the estimated value at the end of useful life — a future projection, not the current value.

questions.stem: Which of the following are considered original costs as opposed to operational expenses? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Original costs (acquisition costs) are warranty costs (A), purchase price/lease cost (B), and delivery costs (C) — all paid at the time of acquisition. Operational expenses (D, E, F) are incurred during the ongoing use and maintenance of the asset.

questions.stem: After installing the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) plugin, how do you update it when new versions become available?

options.text: The HI portal team automatically updates as new versions become available
On your instance, filter on application updates, then click Update
On your instance, filter on application updates, then request an update from HI
Run scheduled job, HAM Check for Updates, and request an update
Check the HI portal for updates and request an update

questions.explanation: After installing HAM, when new versions are available, you update by filtering on application updates in your instance and clicking Update (B). This uses the standard ServiceNow application management process for store-delivered plugins.

questions.stem: Baseline ITSM Asset Management provides which features? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline ITSM Asset Management provides Mobile My Assets (A), Stockrooms (F), and Mobile Asset Receiving (G). Hardware Model Normalization (B), Asset Inventory Audit (C), Hardware Asset Dashboard (D), and Lifecycle Dates (E) are exclusive to the HAM plugin. The the docs confirms normalization is a HAM-specific feature.

questions.stem: Taxes paid at the time of purchase are what type of cost?
questions.explanation: Taxes paid at the time of purchase are classified as an Original Cost (D) — part of the initial acquisition cost incurred when the asset is purchased. Original costs are one-time costs at purchase, distinct from ongoing operational expenses.

questions.stem: Within the asset audit form, where would you find the list of all assets that are currently assigned to the stockroom or warehouse that is being audited?
questions.explanation: The 'Expected Assets' section (B) in the asset audit form shows the list of all assets currently assigned to the stockroom or location being audited. The the docs explicitly states: 'Expected Assets: Shows a list of all assets that are part of the stockroom or location that is being audited.'

questions.stem: When a hardware asset is retired what happens to any existing software allocations on that asset?

options.text: The software allocations remain with the hardware asset and need to be reclaimed manually
The software allocations are handled based upon the configuration of the system property glide.ham.retire_sw()
The software allocations are removed from the asset but not returned to inventory
The software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory

questions.explanation: When a hardware asset is retired, software allocations remain with the asset and must be reclaimed manually (A). ServiceNow HAM does not automatically return software allocations to inventory upon asset retirement — this requires a separate reclamation action in SAM.

questions.stem: Which are valid hardware model lifecycle phases? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid hardware model lifecycle phases include General Availability (A), Pre-release (D), and End of Life (F). The the docs shows General Availability and End of Life as standard hardware lifecycle phases. Upgrade (B), End of Subscription (C), and Beta (E) are not standard hardware model lifecycle phase types in HAM.

questions.stem: What functionality enables you to automatically create asset records from information provided by your vendor while your assets are still in transit?
questions.explanation: Advanced Shipment Notification (ASN) (A) automatically creates asset records from vendor-provided information while assets are still in transit. The the docs confirms: 'Use Advanced Shipment Notification (ASN) to automate and create asset records when your assets are in transit.'

questions.stem: During an audit, when is the Scanned Assets related list updated in the asset audit form?

options.text: When the nightly scheduled job runs
Each time scans are submitted from the app
Every time an item is scanned from the app

questions.explanation: The Scanned Assets related list in the asset audit form is updated each time scans are submitted from the ServiceNow Agent app (D). The the docs confirms: 'The list is updated each time scans are submitted from the ServiceNow Agent app.'

questions.stem: What is an attribute that will remain unchanged throughout the life of the asset?
questions.explanation: CPU type (C) is the attribute that remains unchanged throughout the life of an asset. While memory and OS change with upgrades, and serial number identifies the physical unit, CPU type is the core physical characteristic defining the asset's processing capability throughout its lifecycle.

questions.stem: During the hardware model normalization process, which field is the most important criteria for creating a fully Normalized hardware model?
questions.explanation: Manufacturer (C) is the most important criteria for creating a fully normalized hardware model. The the docs states: 'For a model to be fully normalized, you must add manufacturer details.' Manufacturer is the top-level normalization field — without it, no normalization can occur at all.

questions.stem: Key features of consumables are: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Key features of consumables are that they are managed in bulk/quantities (B) rather than individually tracked by serial number, and they typically have low value (E) which is why they are not individually serialized. Consumables cannot be discovered (A), are not retired on consumption (C) — the record remains for reporting.

questions.stem: What baseline flow could you use to replace hardware assets nearing their end-of-life?
questions.explanation: The 'Hardware Asset Refresh' (C) is the baseline flow used to replace hardware assets nearing their end-of-life. The the docs confirms: 'Request a Hardware Asset Refresh — Use the Hardware Refresh request flow to track aged hardware assets nearing end of life cycle.'

questions.stem: Fixed assets refer to what type of assets?
questions.explanation: Fixed assets refer to long-term assets (D) — assets not intended for quick conversion to cash. The the docs confirms fixed assets are 'commonly tracked at the corporate level by finance or accounting' as capital assets on the balance sheet.

questions.stem: Which single view of the Hardware Asset Workspace provides a consolidated set of quick links to manage model normalization, asset requests, transfer orders, stock orders, refresh requests, and disposal orders?
questions.explanation: The Hardware asset overview (A) view provides a consolidated set of quick links to manage model normalization, asset requests, transfer orders, stock orders, refresh requests, and disposal orders. The the docs -1130 explicitly lists all these navigation quick links in the overview.

questions.stem: When an employee leaves a company and their manager submits an Asset Reclamation Request for them which of their assigned assets are reclaimed by default?

options.text: All hardware and software assets but not consumable assets
All hardware, software, and consumable assets selected in the reclaim asset service catalog
All hardware software and consumable assets
All hardware and software assets selected in the reclaim asset service catalog

questions.explanation: When an employee leaves, the manager submits a Reclaim Asset request via Service Catalog, and all hardware and software assets selected in the reclaim asset service catalog (D) are reclaimed by default. The the docs confirms the Reclaim Asset catalog item allows selecting which hardware and software assets to reclaim. Consumables cannot be reclaimed.

questions.stem: What does the depreciation effective date field modify on the depreciation tab? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The depreciation effective date field modifies the Residual date (B), Depreciated amount (C), and Residual value (D) on the depreciation tab. These three fields are calculated by the system based on the effective date, depreciation method, and salvage value. Salvage value (A) is a user input, not calculated from the effective date.

questions.stem: What is the second tier of the capability blueprint?
questions.explanation: The second tier of the capability blueprint is Practical management (A). The four tiers in order are: Tier 1=Trustworthy data, Tier 2=Practical management, Tier 3=Operational integration, Tier 4=Financial management.

questions.stem: Which are assets? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: From the options, Servers (A - hardware asset), Software entitlements (B), and Facilities (E) are assets tracked in ServiceNow ITAM. Software distributions (C) are installation media, not tracked assets. Network cables (D) are consumables but not standard individual IT assets in this context.

questions.stem: Which view within the Hardware Asset Management Workspace enables Asset Managers to work on features such as RMA request lines asset audits, disposal orders and stock orders?
questions.explanation: The Inventory view (C) within the Hardware Asset Management Workspace enables asset managers to work on RMA request lines, asset audits, disposal orders, and stock orders. The the docs confirms the Inventory overview includes open RMA request lines, asset audits, and stock order data.

questions.stem: What information would you find on me Model Management tab of me Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Hardware models up for end of life
Hardware model purchase orders pending delivery
New hardware assets found by audits

questions.explanation: The Model Management tab shows Hardware model normalization status (B) and Hardware models up for end of life (C). The the docs and confirm this tab covers normalization status, lifecycle overview, and end-of-life data. Expenditure by vendor (D) is on the Procurement tab; new assets from audits (F) is on the Inventory tab.

questions.stem: What is required to manage utilization of the Hardware Asset Management Content Service?

options.text: The service must be opted in to and can be opted out of in the future, if required.
The service must be opted in to, but once enabled it cannot be opted out of.
A script must be defined to identify what information should be shared with the Content Service.
Nothing. The service is atomically enabled and cannot be opted out of.
The service is automatically enabled through the baseline installation but can be opted out of, if required.

questions.explanation: Managing the HAM Content Service requires explicitly opting in, and the service can be opted out of in the future if required (A). Navigate to Asset > Administration > Hardware Model Normalization > Content Service Setup to opt in. The service is not automatic (D, E) and can be opted out of after enabling (B is wrong).

questions.stem: What is the first tier of the capability blueprint?
questions.explanation: The first tier of the ITAM Capability Blueprint is Trustworthy Data (C). The four tiers progress: Tier 1 (Trustworthy Data) → Tier 2 (Practical Management) → Tier 3 (Operational Integration) → Tier 4 (Strategic Conformance). Trustworthy data is foundational — without clean data, higher-tier capabilities cannot be achieved. Financial management (E) is not a tier.

questions.stem: Populating CMDB tables using import sets can inadvertently result in duplicate configuration items (CIs). To minimize this duplication, you can apply what process to the import sets?
questions.explanation: To minimize duplicate CIs when populating CMDB via import sets, apply the Identification and Reconciliation (C) process. The IRE (Identification and Reconciliation Engine) identifies existing CI records before creating new ones, matching incoming data to existing CIs to prevent duplication. Import set prioritization (A) and transform map consolidation (D) do not address deduplication.
